text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Income taxes turned downward this year and will be two percent lower next year, tax-payer association says.
- Social welfare and health expenditures of Finnish municipalities continue to grow, exceeding budget estimates by 4-5 percent, says Association of Finnish Local Authorities.
- Majority of young Finnsh people say their foreign language skills are good.
- Prime Minster Paavo Lipponen accused media of overplaying reports of his recent heart rhythm problem.
- Interior minister Jan-Erik Enestam blames Estonia police for being soft on illicit drugs.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Chief financial officers of 12 major Finnish corporations say Sweden's stance on EMU is crucial in deciding pros and cons of monetary union.

- Ahlstrom CEO Krister Ahlstrom blames anti-EMU politicians for raising euro-scare, saying EMU is a central element of effort to make European industry capable of competiting with U.S. and Asian industry.
- Nokia plans to use Sun Microsystems Java programming language in some future products, technology director Juhani Kuusi says.
- Salomon Brothers seeks strong foothold in Nordic region.
AAMULEHTI

- Government's draft programme on immigrants would force refugees to take courses in Finnish language and culture to qualify for social benefits. Interior Minister Jan-Erik Enestam would be ready to double Finland's refugee quota.
- UPM-Kymmene's new Tervasaari paper mill cost the company 10 percent less than budgeted to build.
- Italian opera tenor Luciano Pavarotti to sing in Helsinki a year from now. Best seats to cost 1,500 markka each.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Olof Salmen, a farmer's son from Finland's Aland Islands, chosen new president of Nordic Council.
- Finns are very conscientious about paying their bills, says spokesman for "Guarantee Fund", which helps those who fall on hard times meet their financial obligations.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 235
